ip_top_stories.title: Authors Sue Meta's AI Scientists Directly in Llama Copyright Case
ip_top_stories.summary: Authors have filed suit directly against Meta's AI scientists in the ongoing Llama copyright litigation, escalating the legal battle beyond the company itself. The move represents a notable shift in litigation strategy, targeting individual researchers rather than just the corporate entity. The case centres on allegations that Meta's Llama models were trained on copyrighted works without authorisation.

ip_top_stories.title: UMG and Sony seek to add over 61k recordings to Suno lawsuit after discovery reveals AI trained on 'millions' of their copyrighted tracks
ip_top_stories.summary: Universal Music Group and Sony Music are seeking to dramatically expand their lawsuit against AI music generator Suno, adding over 61,000 recordings after discovery proceedings allegedly revealed that the AI was trained on millions of their copyrighted tracks. The development significantly broadens the scope of the case and the potential damages at stake. The lawsuit is one of the most consequential AI music copyright cases currently before US courts.

ip_top_stories.title: MiniMax loses bid to dismiss Disney copyright lawsuit over AI system
ip_top_stories.summary: A US court has rejected Chinese AI company MiniMax's attempt to dismiss a copyright lawsuit brought by Disney and Warner Bros., allowing the case to proceed. The suit alleges that MiniMax's AI system infringed on the studios' copyrighted content. The ruling is a significant procedural win for major entertainment rights holders pursuing AI copyright claims.

ip_top_stories.title: Sony Music Files to Expand Udio Suit, Alleges 30K Infringed Works
ip_top_stories.summary: Sony Music has filed to expand its lawsuit against AI music platform Udio, now alleging infringement across 30,000 works. The expansion follows ongoing discovery and adds to the growing body of major label litigation targeting AI audio generation platforms. The case runs parallel to the Suno proceedings and collectively represents a major front in music industry copyright enforcement against AI.

ip_top_stories.title: Artist Sues Copyright Office Over its Refusal to Register His AI-Enhanced Photo
ip_top_stories.summary: An artist has filed suit against the US Copyright Office after it refused to register his AI-enhanced photograph, challenging the agency's position on copyright eligibility for human-AI collaborative works. The case could have significant implications for how copyright protection is determined when AI tools are involved in the creative process. It adds to a growing body of litigation testing the boundaries of copyright law in the context of AI-assisted art.

ip_further_links.title: OpenAI Must Produce Testimony From Musk Case in Copyright Suits
ip_further_links.summary: A court has ordered OpenAI to produce testimony from the Elon Musk litigation for use in separate copyright infringement suits, potentially broadening the evidentiary record against the company.

ip_further_links.title: Can you own a voice? Taylor Swift's latest legal move raises big questions for AI and copyright
ip_further_links.summary: Taylor Swift's legal action over AI voice replication is raising broader questions about whether and how copyright and trademark law can protect a performer's voice from AI reproduction.

ip_further_links.title: Media orgs push back against the relaxation of federal government's stance on AI, copyright
ip_further_links.summary: Media organisations are opposing moves by the US federal government to soften its position on AI and copyright, arguing that relaxed rules would undermine creators' rights.

ip_further_links.title: Mind the Gap: States Step in to Address Ownership of AI-Generated Works Amid Federal Uncertainty
ip_further_links.summary: With federal copyright law slow to address AI-generated works, US states are beginning to introduce their own legislation to fill the gap on ownership questions.

ip_further_links.title: Copyright and Artificial Intelligence: the UK's pivot towards a new digital replica right
ip_further_links.summary: Analysis of the UK government's emerging policy shift toward introducing a new digital replica right as part of its approach to AI and copyright reform.

ip_further_links.title: Japan eyes rules to regulate AI summaries' 'free riding' on news
ip_further_links.summary: Japan is considering regulatory measures to prevent AI systems from freely summarising news content without compensation to publishers, as part of broader efforts to protect media organisations.

ip_further_links.title: Matt Comyn urges Australia to resolve AI copyright standoff
ip_further_links.summary: Commonwealth Bank of Australia chief Matt Comyn has called on the Australian government to break the deadlock over AI and copyright, warning that regulatory uncertainty is impeding the technology sector.

ip_further_links.title: EU Call for Evidence Targets Generative AI's Impact on Copyright
ip_further_links.summary: The EU has launched a call for evidence examining the impact of generative AI on copyright, forming part of a broader review of how existing rules apply to AI-generated and AI-trained content.

ip_further_links.title: Creative industries fight push to change copyright laws
ip_further_links.summary: Creative industry groups are actively opposing proposed changes to copyright legislation that they argue would weaken protections for human creators in favour of AI developers.

ip_further_links.title: Legal Risk Could Deflate the GenAI Bubble
ip_further_links.summary: Analysis argues that mounting copyright litigation and unresolved legal liability around training data could pose a systemic risk to the valuations and business models underpinning the generative AI sector.
